messages:
support_jess: heads up — we have an escalation from AcmeHealth on dedicated pool redwood-dedicated-eu-a. High p95 latency and a bunch of 429s since ~10:05 UTC. customer sees throughput drop ~3x. ticket #INC-4729. attaching short logs and customer repro.

maria: thx Jess. do we have batcher metrics? token/batch distribution?

aj: pulling grafana now — looks like batch size median collapsed from ~900 tokens -> ~120 tokens around 10:04. p99 latency jumped right after. link: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/batcher?orgId=1&panelId=22 (embedding snapshot)

ryan: weird — there was a runtime config roll yesterday 03:30 UTC touching continuous-batcher defaults. rollout id: r-deploy-2026-03-16-22. could be related. deploy-bot shows the change: 
```
changed: continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens: 2048 -> 256
changed: continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms: 100 -> 250
```

maria: Oof. lowering max_batch_tokens to 256 would definitely fragment batches for our tokeny workloads. That explains throughput drop and more 429s because scheduler gets many small batches and throughput drops, hitting per-pool qps.

support_jess: customer also reported retries spiking and a couple of billing anomalies (retry loop causing duplicate billable tokens). ops flagged that separately but likely downstream of throttles.

aj: checking autoscaler logs — HPA for batcher pods scaled from 12 -> 4 at 09:58, then back to 10 by 10:20. scaling decisions look based on cpu% threshold (50%). But CPU/latency mismatch here since more small batches -> higher scheduling overhead but not high CPU per pod, so HPA underscaled. HPA events: 
```
Event: scaling from 12 to 4, reason: cpu below threshold (avg 42%)
```

maria: so two issues compounded: (1) config rollback lowered max_batch_tokens causing fragmentation, (2) HPA tuned to CPU only so it scaled down during the fragmentation window and made queues back up -> 429s.

ryan: repro steps I used locally:
1) push continuous-batcher config with max_batch_tokens=256 to canary
2) run synthetic load of 10k requests/min with avg 600 tokens/request
3) observe batch size distribution and p95 tokens/sec drop

logs:
```
[10:03:58] batcher: created 38 batches size=[30,12,50,...] total_tokens=7200
[10:04:04] scheduler: queued 1200 requests, latency p95=820ms
[10:04:10] api: returning 429 throttle: pool_capacity_exceeded request_id=rid-9f3b
```

aj: mitigation plan: revert max_batch_tokens to 2048 in the runtime config (immediate), restart batcher pods in that pool to pick up config, temporarily pin HPA minReplicas=10 for redwood-dedicated-eu-a until we can switch autoscaling metric to request-based or queue-length based metric.

support_jess: can you do the revert and pin? Customer wants ETA and we need a public response. I'll draft support reply once we have ETA. :pray:

ryan: rolling config revert to canary now, will promote to prod pool after 2 successful minutes in canary. deploy-bot: r-deploy-2026-03-17-02 revert-max-batch-tokens -> canary started.

deploy-bot: deploy r-deploy-2026-03-17-02 progressed: canary success (2m). staging -> prod promotion queued.

aj: also opened infra task to change HPA to use custom metric queue_length_per_pod and to set minReplicas=8 for dedicated pools by default: INFRA-1257.

maria: followups: (a) run a regression test against high-token workloads for next deploy, (b) add a pre-deploy check to warn if max_batch_tokens decreased >50% for pools with >200 average tokens/request, (c) check billing duplicates for customer. I'll own (a) and (b).

support_jess: thanks all. I sent customer a note: "we identified a config regression and are reverting; expect improvement within 10-15min; we'll follow up with a postmortem and billing correction if needed."

ryan: prod revert in progress. will update here when pool metrics show median batch size back to ~900.

support_jess: closing loop later — please ping me once metrics stable so I can update ticket INC-4729. :white_check_mark:
